DESCRIBES the family's history and the state of its documents. Checked: the Go and TypeScript surface documents exist under their stacks' spec/*/tools/, and until this file landed the Rust directory held only two TCG documents — the measurement that opened B-051.

DESCRIBES, and it is the document's first strong claim, verified rather than assumed: rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/Cargo.toml declares only library dependencies (conform-core, specmark, proc-macro2, quote, syn) — no process spawn, no bridge crate — while the Go and TS twins each spawn an extractor over NDJSON. Boss-checked: `syn::parse_file` is called in-process at rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/src/lib.rs:85.
The section's kind line, in the form both sibling surface documents use (`req r1`).
PRESCRIBES the division of labour, coherent and with every referent resolving: cargo build, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check and the test suite are all panel steps in tools/self-check.sh.
PRESCRIBES; the rationale sentence of the division above, and the twin documents carry the identical clause for their own toolchains.
The lead-in to the rule roster; its list is judged bullet by bullet below.

DESCRIBES a measured asymmetry between two rule rosters. Checked: Go carries one `RULE-BAN-CENSUS-AS-FACTS` umbrella and one `go-seam-error-cites-req`, where the Rust roster splits both — the ids on each side are those returned by the rules' own `impl Rule::id`. Boss-verified independently of the worker's report, 2026-08-05: `grep 'fn id(&self)' -A2` over core-ai-native-conform/src/rules/*.rs returns 24 rule ids; the 14 named in this document are exactly the non-`go-`/`ts-` subset, and `lint-suppression-needs-reason` is the 15th wired rule, fed by SARIF rather than by rust-syn — which is why the document carries it outside the list.
PRESCRIBES the reason the frontends route through one engine; the identical clause stands in the Go surface document, and the shared `conform_core::Fact` it names is the type every frontend emits.
The section's kind line, in the sibling documents' form.
DESCRIBES the frontend's contract: `extract(file, package, module, text) -> Vec<Fact>`, the `Frontend` trait method implemented at rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/src/lib.rs:48-87.
DESCRIBES; the same measurement that carries `##NO-SIDECAR-IS-THE-STRUCTURAL-DIFFERENCE` — a library call, no subprocess, no materialised extractor.

DESCRIBES, and it is asserted by a compiled doctest rather than by prose: rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/src/lib.rs:43-44 asserts `RustFrontend.extract("x.rs","demo","demo","fn (").is_empty()`, and the implementation returns an empty Vec on a `syn::parse_file` error at :85-87.

DESCRIBES the emitted vocabulary. Checked against the `extract` implementation and its visitor: ten variants are constructed there (FileMetrics, Item, Import, Ctor, UnsafeUse, ErrorVariant, UnwrapUse, EnvRead, InvariantComment, TestSweep); the Ts*/Go* variants of the shared enum and `LintDiagnosis` are not, and the document says so.

DESCRIBES, and it refutes the Go twin's claim rather than inheriting it. Boss-verified: `syn::parse_file` appears at core-ai-native-specmap/src/rscan.rs:267 AND at rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/src/lib.rs:85 — two crates, two parses over the same text, one emitting CodeItem/Edge for the index and the other Fact for the rules. The anchor was renamed from the twin's `ONE-EXTRACTION-TWO-CONSUMERS` because the inherited name asserted the opposite of the measurement.
The section's kind line, in the sibling documents' form.
DESCRIBES the trait implementation: `impl Frontend for RustFrontend` with `id()`, `version()` and `extract()` at rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/src/lib.rs:48-87.

DESCRIBES. Boss-verified: `fn version()` returns "10" at rust-ai-native-conform-frontend/src/lib.rs:81, and the comment block above it records v2-v10, every entry a change to what the extraction emits or a narrowing of an existing fact's scope — which is the sentence's claim about WHY it bumps.

The section's kind line, in the sibling documents' form.

DESCRIBES the `[rust]` schema. PRESCRIBES the consequence of the boundary above; every referent resolves.
PRESCRIBES, citing ENGINE-CONFORM §1, whose tier section defines T-lex / T-syn / T-sem and resolves.

DESCRIBES, and it is a correction of the draft's strongest claim rather than its confirmation. Boss-verified: `Fact::LintDiagnosis` exists at core-ai-native-conform/src/facts.rs:246, the root `sarif_reports` key at config.rs:140, and `sarif::load_reports` is called by the Rust gate at rust-ai-native-conform/src/lib.rs:147 — so clippy diagnoses are read back in as facts and the tier is not empty. PRESCRIBES the placement rule. Coherent and matched by the live schema: the four root keys model no language, and the three language tables are homogeneous — each owns its own roots/gated/exempt shape (RustConfig, TsConfig, GoConfig in the same file).
